themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models keep starting by building a small truth set of their own, or by admitting the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization the models say drift is bigger than any effect they could cause, on cross-channel incrementality they say platforms change the baseline mid-flight, on identity resolution they say nobody has a verified answer key for who is the same person, and on B2B buying-group signal loss they say a dead signal and a signal that never worked look identical.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blocker is often money and politics, inside the company as well as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: Today on cross-channel journey orchestration all three models point at channel teams whose bonuses reward sending more, echoing the agent traffic answers that offer bots a faster lane so declaring beats hiding, and the semantic context layer answers that call conflicting definitions a political fight over whose number changes.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Safe agent execution draws proxies, gateways, and dry-run checks from all three models, downstream consent draws a single egress checkpoint, and today's journey orchestration answers propose one shared contact log or suppression rule that every channel must check before sending.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch behavior from the outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion the models call ad platforms and trained models black boxes with no accepted test for removal, on incrementality they say platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, and on answer engines they say there is no index or log to read.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning, context, and what counts as a good outcome, and no rule set captures that fully. So the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance comes down to whether a phrase crosses into a misleading claim, the semantic context layer answers argue plural meanings of customer are legitimate and should be disclosed rather than merged, and today's orchestration answers say globally optimal has no definition anyone can commit to.
